newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's ABI sees room for interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Italy's ABI sees room for interest rate cut.

text.p: The president of Italy's banking association (ABI) Tancredi Bianchi said on Tuesday that there is room for a further fall in Italian interest rates this year, but the timing should be left to the Bank of Italy.
Bianchi was speaking at a news conference after a meeting with the government on labour costs in the banking industry.

"There is space, not big, for a fall in short term rates and therefore the discount rate, of around one full percentage point this year, but....the Bank of Italy needs to be left to continue on the road it has undertaken, that has produced these good results," Bianchi said.

Italian consumer price inflation has been falling steadily over the last year, and fell to 2.2 percent year-on-year in March from February's 2.4 percent, and from 4.5 percent in March 1996. It has now reached the lowest level since May 1969.
The Bank of Italy has twice cut the discount rate in the past year, each time by 75 basis points, in response to falls in inflation. The official discount rate is now 6.75 percent.

Bianchi said that the Bank of Italy is determined to prevent inflation rising, and added that it would be foolish to cut rates and then find the lira slipping to around 1,020 lire against the German mark.
The lira was last quoted around 986 lire per mark.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said at the weekend that Italian CPI would fall to 1.9 percent in April and could dip to 1.5 percent by June. The government has set a target of annual average inflation of 2.5 percent for 1997.
